name: Canyon_Resource_Indicators
description: Visual hints of resources embedded in rock types — ore veins, crystal seams, fossil deposits visible in canyon walls

questions.question: Can the player learn to associate specific rock types with potential resources such as basalt yielding iron or limestone indicating cave systems?
Would a screenshot showing visible ore veins and crystal seams embedded in canyon walls be a compelling discovery marketing image?
Do resource indicators appear naturally embedded in strata such as veins, nodules, crystal seams, and fossil bands rather than floating UI markers?
Can resource indicators be implemented using existing UE5 decal actor systems or material-layer overrides without new C++ components?
Do resource indicators require a new resource-data model or can they use the existing geology module rock-type taxonomy?
Are detailed resource-vein indicators using nanite-favorable geometry compatible with UE5.8 virtual texture streaming?
Can resource indicator decals and overlay geometry be rendered without exceeding 50 extra draw calls per canyon vista?
Can colorblind players distinguish resource indicators via shape differences, shimmer effects, or tooltip descriptions?
Do resource-rich rock surfaces produce a distinct scanning ping or mining-impact sound compared to barren rock?
Are resource indicator placements deterministic and consistent across all clients so every player sees the same vein at the same spot?
Can the community define new resource types and their corresponding visual indicators through data configs without touching C++?
Are resource names, tooltip descriptions, mineral identifiers, and gather instructions stored in localization tables?
Do resource indicators depend on the geology module having a complete rock-type taxonomy with resource-association mappings?
Do resource indicators prove that the environmental demo produces actionable gameplay consequences via a gather-loop?
Is this derived from the educational principle that visual geology knowledge should produce tangible gameplay rewards?
Do colorful resource indicators visually clutter the canyon wall or distract from the educational strata layers they sit on top of?
What art-pipeline knowledge (decal authoring, material layering, mesh LODs) is needed to author resource-vein indicators?
Do resource indicators serve the seed goal of exploration-driven gameplay where observation yields real gameplay advantage?
What visual subtlety is sacrificed if resource indicators are 2D decals rather than embedded 3D vein geometry?
How do we know that visual resource indicators actually motivate players to learn rock types rather than just mining every visible vein?
Does the chain see indicator -> identify resource -> harvest -> use reach a human player making a deliberate gameplay decision?
Does this need deeper sub-features such as a resource scanner tool, minimap overlay, or extraction animations, or are static indicators sufficient?
Are sibling resource features missing such as a resource map, portable scanner device, or extraction spot animations?
Is Demo_Canyon_Terrain specific enough about resource gameplay to fully scope these indicators without reopening parent questions?
Should resource indicators be built after strata visuals since they render on top of visible rock layers?
Does incomplete resource indicators block the gathering gameplay loop, or can gathering work with text labels while indicators are built?
